target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ (𝓢 : ArithmeticTheory) (K F : ArithmeticSentence → ArithmeticSentence),
    Def1 (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) K ∧ (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) ⪯ 𝓢 ∧
    Def2 𝓢 K ∧ Def3 𝓢 K ∧ Def4 𝓢 K ∧
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ)) ∧
    ¬ 𝓢 ⊢ K (∼K (∼F ⊥))

translation: Target is defined to be the proposition that there exist an arithmetic theory 𝓢 and two functions K and F, in that order, from closed arithmetic sentences to closed arithmetic sentences, such that all of the following hold for those same choices: (1) For every sentence φ, if PA proves φ, then PA proves K(φ). (2) Every sentence PA proves is also proved by 𝓢. (3) For every sentence φ and every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves K(φ → ψ) → (K(φ) → K(ψ)). (4) For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(φ) → φ. (5) For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) → φ). (6) For every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) → F(φ)). (7) 𝓢 does not prove K(¬K(¬F(⊥))). Here → and ¬ inside sentences are arithmetic-language connectives, and ⊥ is the falsehood sentence. The last condition is nonprovability, not a requirement that 𝓢 prove the negation of the displayed sentence. Condition (1) concerns PA; no analogous closure condition is imposed on 𝓢. Neither function is required to be given by a formula, and no Def5 fixed-point condition is imposed.

divergences.description: The passage says that every instance satisfying Theorem 4’s hypotheses yields S ⊢ K¬K(Con(F)). The target asserts the existence of an instance of modified hypotheses in which that conclusion is not provable. The passage makes no claim about the necessity of a proviso in such a variant.

The passage requires S to include EA and uses its designated K. The target instead takes an ordinary arithmetic theory extending PA in theoremhood and chooses a sentence function K subject to PA-necessitation, distribution, factivity, and known factivity. These are conditions on a chosen function, not the requirement that S include EA.

The passage requires a single formula F(x) of the object language, applied to the code of each sentence. Although F(x) need not be Σ⁰₁, it must still be a formula. The target allows any function on arithmetic sentences, with no requirement that its values be instances of one formula.

judgement.summary: The target accurately expresses the author’s stated counterexample claim about the modified setting. That claim is additional to the passage, and a witness to it would not by itself refute the printed theorem.
